speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) receives complaints, tip-offs and referrals from members of public as well as other public agencies on possible illegal employment of work pass holders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Based on the information received, MOM will conduct inspections and look into each and every allegation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: At the same time, MOM also carries out proactive inspections based on our own analysis and triggers to detect possible illegal employment of work pass holders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM takes a serious view of illegal employment.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just a quick clarification, in terms of the things that are being done to ensure compliance and to enforce that there is no moonlighting involved, I am just wondering how has the approach that the Ministry has taken evolved over the last five years, in terms of improving its processes to ensure that these cases are being picked up.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: A lot of them would be part-time in nature without necessarily any documentation involved.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: A very recent example would be the KTV cluster where a number of them would have committed offences under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Engagement and education of the migrant workers are done through several other initiatives and platforms.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, the mobile app, FWMOMCare, where MOM pushes out employment-related messages through the app.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it really is to help foreign workers themselves know what is illegal and wrong.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There is also the mandatory Settling-in Programme for first-time work permit holders, which educates the migrant workers on their responsibilities and employment rights as well as the laws and regulations for working in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Prior to COVID-19, we did conduct a lot of road shows as well, at dormitories, at recreation centres, in public areas, where MOM would engage these work pass holders on their rights and responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Of course, in the present day, we utilise a lot of social media platforms and the online medium to educate and raise awareness.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And if we do have enforcement actions being taken, especially against companies who were egregious, we do publicise them on the mainstream media as well as online social media platforms because this raises awareness and serve as a deterrence to other would-be offenders – whether it is employers or employees.
